label: Plain English medieval terms
summary: Every title in the kingdom's vocabulary must be a word a reader recognizes without a glossary; flavor never beats clarity.
quote: Every title must be a word a person recognizes without a glossary

label: Raw data in, structure out
summary: A contradiction in what the Regent enters is a missing fact to hunt down, never a rule violation to scold him for.
quote: A contradiction is a missing fact to be hunted, never a rule violation to be scolded.

label: Lordlessness is a reading, not an error
summary: A fief exists whether or not it has a lord; an empty seat is data the gauge reports, never a fault the system raises.
quote: The fief exists whether or not it has a lord. An empty seat is data.

label: Deliberate acts, recorded
summary: Authority exists only through recorded acts — grants and appointments — which is what separates a lord who rules several fiefs from a regent buried under them.
quote: Authority exists only through recorded acts — grants and appointments.

label: The system hunts delegation debt
summary: Any time someone is doing a job they should be delegating, the board says so — the instrument the whole panel exists to serve.
quote: Any time someone is doing a job they should be delegating, the board says so.

label: Actions stand beside their information
summary: Anything on screen that names a thing is a road to that thing, and undoing or continuing a recorded act is offered right where the record is shown.
quote: Anything on screen that names a thing is a road to that thing

label: The line of rule
summary: The management chain — delegation authority flows King to Regent to fief lords to their vassals; holding a fief places a person on this line.
quote: Delegation authority flows through it: King → Regent → fief lords → their vassals.

label: The line of trade
summary: Local mastery — a mayor runs a hamlet because they are trusted and expert there, never because they outrank anyone; holding a hamlet is not a rung on the management ladder.
quote: runs a hamlet because they are trusted and expert there, not because they outrank anyone.

label: A fief is a book of doors
summary: A fief is a group's book of doors — the portfolio a lord leads, knights pledge to, and squires are seated in — existing independently of who holds it.
quote: a group's **BOOK OF DOORS**: the portfolio a lord leads, knights pledge to, and squires are seated in.

label: A Crown office is never land
summary: An office has no geometry, never appears on the map, cannot be folded into a fief or raised to one, and no outside artisan may ever keep it.
quote: An office is never land.

label: A hamlet's mayor answers to the fief's lord
summary: A hamlet is a sub-territory inside a fief with a mayor on the line of trade; a mayor is never a Chancellor.
quote: The mayor answers to the fief's lord. A mayor is never a Chancellor.

label: A guild is an outside trade the Crown does not staff
summary: A guild is an outside trade (roofers, lenders, counsel); the Crown does not staff or man one, and its hands are artisans.
quote: The Crown does not staff a guild and cannot "man" one; its hands are **artisans**.

label: A garrison is worked land without local leadership
summary: A garrison is not a territory type so much as a condition — artisans stationed in a territory with no local leadership.
quote: Not a territory type so much as a condition: worked land without local leadership.

label: The graduation path
summary: A garrison becomes a hamlet when it gets a mayor; a hamlet becomes a fief when the kingdom grows enough to need it sovereign. A Crown office walks neither way.
quote: a garrison becomes a hamlet when it gets a mayor; a hamlet becomes a fief when the kingdom grows enough to need it sovereign.

label: The board is drawn flat, definitively
summary: The realm map is authored 2D art composited in the browser, not a live 3D scene and not a photographic render — a head-to-head test decided it.
quote: The board is drawn FLAT — 2D illustration, definitively (ratified — Edwin, 2026-07-28).

label: The land itself is invented
summary: The realm the war table draws is a fantasy realm, not a real county — retired from a brief period as a baked survey of real ground.
quote: The land itself is INVENTED (ratified — Edwin, 2026-07-28).

label: Generated land may never be presented as a finding
summary: The doors carry the data; the ground is scenery. A gap or cluster drawn on invented terrain says nothing true about drive time, vendor radius or concentration risk.
quote: generated land may never be presented as a finding.

label: Lorded — an internal vassal holds it by grant
summary: The healthy of the four fief states: an internal vassal holds the fief by explicit grant.
quote: an internal vassal holds it by explicit grant. Healthy.

label: Held in plurality — legitimate, watched, not flagged
summary: One vassal holding several fiefs, each by explicit grant, is legitimate and historically normal — watched, not flagged as debt.
quote: one vassal holds several fiefs, each by explicit grant. Legitimate and historically normal. Watched, not flagged.

label: In regency — a recorded keeper runs it
summary: No vassal lord, but a recorded keeper (an artisan formally appointed) runs the fief day-to-day — the kingdom's work gets done, but by foreign hands. Amber.
quote: no vassal lord; a recorded **keeper** (an artisan formally appointed to keep the castle for its absent lord) runs it day-to-day.

label: In stewardship — everything undelegated falls to the Regent
summary: No grant, no appointment, nothing recorded: everything undelegated under the Crown falls to the Regent, not as a holding but as a thing that needs delegating. Red.
quote: everything undelegated under the Crown falls to the Regent — not as a holding, but as a thing that needs delegating.

label: The Regent's desk is the red-flag instrument
summary: Every fief in stewardship appears on the Regent's desk as open delegation debt, whose ideal length is zero.
quote: The desk is the red-flag instrument: its ideal length is zero.

label: A grant places a vassal in charge, dated
summary: A grant places an internal vassal in charge of a territory — role lord for a fief, mayor for a hamlet.
quote: places an internal vassal in charge of a territory. Role *lord* for a fief (line of rule), *mayor* for a hamlet (line of trade). Dated.

label: A keeper appointment names a day-to-day artisan
summary: Formally names an artisan as day-to-day keeper of a territory that has no lord — the distinction between regency and stewardship.
quote: formally names an artisan as day-to-day keeper of a territory that has no lord.

label: A garrison posting is workforce, not authority
summary: Stations an artisan in a territory as workforce — the record carries no authority.
quote: stations an artisan in a territory as workforce. Not authority.

label: Fealty records service under a fief's lord
summary: Records a vassal serving inside a fief under its lord.
quote: records a vassal serving inside a fief under its lord.

label: Presence in the book is the only truth
summary: Striking a person leaves the records that name them in their books; the readings tolerate the gap because a dangling record is a fact about the past, not an error in the present.
quote:
presence in the book is the only truth and
a dangling record is a fact about the past, not an error in the present.

label: Re-pledging: pledges can change, records survive
summary: A squire is knighted a vassal, an artisan is hired inside the walls, a squire's knight can change — records survive the change and the readings recompute around it.
quote: a squire is knighted a vassal, an artisan is hired inside the walls (the mission's own arc: foreign hands becoming subjects), a squire's knight can change.

label: Graduation: a hamlet promotes, a fief can fold
summary: A hamlet is promoted to a sovereign fief, and a fief can be folded back inside another as a hamlet; records survive the move, and a stray record is shown where it lies, never silently deleted.
quote: a hamlet is **promoted** to a sovereign fief (it opens in whatever state its records say — usually stewardship, straight onto the desk, which is the gauge working)

label: The court opens: acts made and struck in-app
summary: Grants and keeper appointments are made and struck in the app, where the record is shown — a fief's page offers the grant, the appointment, and the revocation beside the seat they concern.
quote: Grants and keeper appointments are made and struck **in the app**, where the record is shown (law 6)

label: The Marches are the border lands
summary: Work that has arrived in the kingdom but has not yet been assigned to any fief; everything enters through the Marches and must be ridden out or turned away.
quote: work that has arrived in the kingdom but has not yet been assigned to any fief

label: Arrival — something new logged at the border
summary: An arrival is something new logged at the border, dated.
quote: something new logged at the border. Dated.

label: Dispatch — riding an arrival out to a territory
summary: The deliberate act of riding an arrival out to a territory, dated; dispatched work appears on the receiving territory's page.
quote: the deliberate act of riding an arrival out to a territory (fief or hamlet).

label: Turnaway — refusing an arrival at the border
summary: The deliberate act of refusing an arrival as no business of the kingdom's, kept in the record book.
quote: the deliberate act of refusing an arrival as no business of the kingdom's.

label: The border scribe only suggests
summary: The scribe reads raw text against the census and pre-fills a destination, but every reading is computed fresh and nothing it says is stored — deliberately conservative, better silent than wrong.
quote: It is deliberately conservative — a sentence never reads as names; better silent than wrong.

label: A deployment is not reachable until an identity wall stands
summary: Wall first, route second, deploy third, verify fourth — and the verification is from a logged-out browser, confirming the wall answers rather than the app.
quote: A deployment is not reachable until an identity wall stands in front of it.

label: The Worker verifies the wall, never trusts a header
summary: A proxy header is only an assertion by whoever last touched the request; with no wall configured the Worker refuses its private APIs outright.
quote: The Worker verifies the wall's assertions; it never trusts a header.

label: No credential is ever version-controlled
summary: Keys reach a deployment through its secret store and a machine through a gitignored .env; only the wall's team domain and audience tag are deliberately version-controlled.
quote: No credential is ever version-controlled.

label: The Treasury keeps upkeep, records in readings out
summary: Version one keeps upkeep — the recurring monthly cost of the kingdom's structure: retainers, salaries, subscriptions, dues.
quote: Version one keeps **upkeep** — the recurring monthly cost of the kingdom's structure: retainers, salaries, subscriptions, dues.

label: The kingdom keeps two treasuries, never confused
summary: The estates in trust (the AppFolio dimension) and the Crown's own coin (the QuickBooks dimension) are kept the way a property manager keeps them — and must never be confused.
quote: The kingdom keeps its books in **two treasuries**, because a property manager does — and they must never be confused

label: The bridge is tribute
summary: Management fees, markups, and leasing fees flow out of the estates' coin and into the Crown's Treasury — the one place the two treasuries meet.
quote: Management fees, markups, and leasing fees flow *out of* the estates' coin and *into* the Crown's Treasury

label: Events-only reaches the operating model
summary: The sole record of the real work is an append-only event log; a work item, a queue, aging and a KPI are all readings folded from it, never stored state.
quote: the sole record is an **append-only event log**.

label: Build general components; a setting loads in
summary: LandLord is the factory building general components; a firm's operating model is a factory setting, kept as a shape that loads in rather than code that hardwires it.
quote: build general components; keep every firm-specific thing as a shape that LOADS IN, never as code that hardwires it.

label: Every archetype gets a clerk agent
summary: Every archetype gets an agent that works its incoming queue as far as it can and stops at the judgment moments for a human click — augment each human, never eliminate.
quote: Every archetype gets an **agent** that works its incoming queue as far as it can and stops at the judgment moments for a human click

label: The Throne fuses the org's and the work's debt
summary: The King's seat sums a fief with no lord and a box with no seat into one number the King drives to zero — the two halves of the instrument built apart.
quote: the sovereign's single screen over the whole realm, fusing the two halves of the instrument that were built apart

label: A task is a word in a bounded language
summary: A task is not an atomic complete click; it is a word in a bounded, compositional language, and each word carries the flow that actually completes it.
quote: it is a **word in a bounded, compositional language, and each word carries the flow that actually completes it.**

label: The gauge is a consequence simulation, not a count
summary: An unattended task festers, escalates into crisis, the Patron loses faith and withdraws, and the coffers bleed until upkeep drowns them — the kingdom falls.
quote: an unattended task **festers → escalates into a crisis → the door's Patron loses faith → the Patron withdraws their doors and their tribute → the coffers bleed until upkeep drowns them → the kingdom falls.**

label: The chronicle binds the Marches and the Treasury into one volume
summary: The kingdom's mutable record books — the Marches ledger and the Treasury rolls — bind into one volume, the chronicle.
quote: the Marches ledger and the Treasury rolls — bind into one volume, the **chronicle**

label: The vault runs row security with no policies
summary: Row security is enabled with no policies, so the public keys open nothing — only the secret key passes, and it lives only in .env or a Worker secret.
quote: row security is enabled with **no policies**, so the public keys open nothing

label: The border book is the only door an outside producer writes through
summary: The chronicle doc is a whole-document write, last writer wins, so a foreign hand writing it directly would clobber the record — a producer drops rows at the border instead.
quote: the **only door an outside producer will ever write through**.

label: A clerk never emits approved or overridden
summary: A clerk stops at the first commitment, emits proposed, and parks the case awaiting — the human's Approve/Override ratchet is the only path forward.
quote: The agent never emits `approved`/`overridden`

label: Only real estate agents may rise through the land
summary: Knights answer to their liege lord, who answers to the King; the three Crown offices serve the land, they do not command it.
quote: Only real estate agents can be knights/fieflords/kings.

label: The org layers are not a downline
summary: The layers of organization are a brokerage's groups and their leads, not MLM overrides — nothing in the economy may be built as a recruitment incentive.
quote: The economics of this are NOT
